Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Africa | Football CAS ruling on Africa Cup of Nations final expected at end of November Source : Reuters 20 October 2026 3:27am Audio By Carbonatix
A decision on Senegal's appeal after being stripped of this year's Africa Cup of Nations title will be made at the end of November, the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) said ​on Monday.
Senegal are contesting the Confederation of African Football's decision to declare Morocco champions , despite ‌Senegal beating the hosts 1-0 after extra time in January's final in Rabat, and their arguments, plus those of Morocco and CAF, were heard by CAS in Lausanne on October 8.
At the time, CAS said it expected a decision within days, but has now decided to issue a complete ruling, including legal grounds, known as a CAS Award.
“This process will require several weeks, with the CAS ⁠Award expected at the end of November 2026,” CAS said in a statement.
Senegal walked off the ​pitch for 14 minutes after a penalty was awarded against them late in regulation time, with several ​players returning to the dressing room in protest before they resumed play.
Morocco missed the spot kick, sending the match into extra time, where Senegal scored the winner to secure victory.
However, they were stripped of the title two months later ​after CAF's Appeal Board ruled that Senegal had forfeited the match by walking off the pitch, ​overturning the result and awarding a 3-0 victory to Morocco.
Senegal quickly followed with an appeal t o sport's highest court CAS, ‌which ⁠was lodged on March 25 but heard some six months later. The basis of their arguments is that the referee’s decision is final and he allowed the match to be completed.
"I know it's a long wait for the fans a few months after the final between Senegal and Morocco,” CAS Director General Matthieu Reeb said outside the hearing earlier this month.
“I expect the decision to come not today, not tomorrow, but a few days later. The facts are set, are clear, and the discussions ​will be on some procedural issues and legal aspects," he added.
The CAS ​panel is ⁠presided over by French sports law expert Gerald Simon, with assistance from Italian international law professor Luigi Fumagalli and Hamburg-based attorney and professor of law at the University of Zurich, Ulrich Haas.
CAS decisions are called awards and have the same value as a national court judgment, enforceable ​under the New York Convention on the Recognition and Enforcement of Foreign Arbitral Awards. CAS awards may be enforced ​by sports federations or state courts, depending on the circumstances.
